text:
mariana: Quick thought — can we define a "canonical bench artifact" for onboarding? Right now different teams run slightly different bench configs and we get divergent perf/correctness baselines.

ben: +1. That would help rollouts. We need a single artifact we can attach to a model entry.

ingrid: Suggest split: tiny smoke for PRs (fast) + canonical full bench for admissions (CI/nightly). Smoke should catch functional regressions, canonical catches perf drift.

sam: Tradeoffs: canonical bench must include stable seeds, tokenization, and deterministic sampling. Hardware noise will still happen — we'll need quantiles and history.

mariana: Draft idea: canonical artifact = {golden_inputs.tar.gz, outputs.norm.gz, perf_trace.pb, manifest.json, tool_version.txt}

alex: Proposed fields in manifest: model_hash, tokenizer_hash, bench_cfg_hash, dataset_version, run_date, p50/p95/p99, exact match checksums, allowed_delta_eps

priyanka: Storage: s3://redwood-artefacts/bench-canon/v1/<model_hash>/

mariana: Example run command:
```
./tools/run_bench --model path/to/model --cfg tests/canonical.yaml --seed 42 --tokens 2048 --out /tmp/canon/
```

dev-bot: Build 7453: queued canonical bench for model: m-glow-7b-2026-03-21

ben: On diffs: allow small output deltas for quantized/FP16 variants. But require a 'golden-hash' for strict regressions.

ingrid: Also require tokenizer pinning. We once had drift due to a tokenizer fix that changed outputs subtly.

sam: Ops question: who owns the artifact lifecycle? Model owner writes manifest, infra publishes and tags artifact immutably.

mariana: Good. I'll put together a short RFC + onboarding checklist with sections: smoke criteria, canonical artifact schema, storage policy, regression thresholds. @ingrid @ben please review tomorrow.

alex: :thumbsup:

priyanka: can help with S3 lifecycle + manifest schema review :+1:

mariana: Thanks — I'll post RFC link here when ready.
